intro: Practice DNS and DHCP: edit records in a simulated DNS console, configure a DHCP scope, and match symptoms to causes.

labs.title: Fix records in a DNS console
labs.summary: Use a DNS Manager console to add, correct and remove records after a server migration.
labs.scenario:
The company's web server moved. The new address is 10.0.0.45. Fix the zone corp.example.com:

  • web01 should point to the new address.
  • www should be a CNAME to web01.corp.example.com (right now it is wrongly an A record to the old address).
  • Add an A record for the new file server files02 at 10.0.0.60.
  • The decommissioned oldmail host should be removed.
  • Before the next change, set the TTL of web01 to 300 seconds.

Edit the table, then Save changes.

tasks.text: files02 exists as an A record to 10.0.0.60
Leave files01 and the MX record unchanged

hints: A CNAME's data is a name, not an IP address.
Change the Type drop-down of the www row to CNAME, then replace the data.
Use Add row for files02, and the delete button on oldmail.
labs.solution: web01: A 10.0.0.45, TTL 300. www: CNAME web01.corp.example.com. Add files02 A 10.0.0.60. Delete oldmail. Save.
labs.review: Moving a service means updating its A record, pointing aliases at the name rather than the address, cleaning up decommissioned hosts and, ideally, lowering the TTL before the change so old answers expire quickly.

labs.title: Configure a DHCP scope
labs.summary: Fix a DHCP scope: correct the range and options, protect static servers with an exclusion and reserve an address for a printer.
labs.scenario:
The new VLAN Accounting uses 192.168.30.0/24. The router is 192.168.30.1 and the DNS server is 192.168.30.5. Static servers use 192.168.30.2 to 192.168.30.20. Clients should get 192.168.30.100 to 192.168.30.200. The printer (MAC AA-BB-CC-11-22-33) must always get 192.168.30.150. Leases for office PCs should be 8 hours.

Fix the scope, then Save changes on each page.

tasks.text: Router option is 192.168.30.1 and DNS is 192.168.30.5

hints: The pool starts at .100, so the static servers at .2 to .20 stay out of it.
Options 003 and 006 are what clients use for their gateway and DNS server.
Add one row to Reservations and fill in all three columns.
labs.solution: Scope: start .100, end .200, lease 8. Router 192.168.30.1, DNS 192.168.30.5, domain corp.local. Reservation: printer, AA-BB-CC-11-22-33, 192.168.30.150.
labs.review: A good scope keeps the dynamic pool away from static addresses, hands out the right gateway and DNS server and uses reservations for devices that need a fixed address. Wrong options are why clients can have an address but no connectivity.

labs.title: Diagnose the symptom
labs.summary: Match symptoms to causes and put the DHCP and DNS steps in order.
labs.scenario: Four tickets came in. Decide what is wrong for each before you start changing things.

activities.title: Symptom to cause
activities.prompt: Drag each symptom to the most likely cause.

items.text: Ping to 8.8.8.8 works but names fail
The site still opens the old server after a move
Clients get an unexpected default gateway from an unknown server
Windows warns that another device uses the same address

activities.title: Resolve a name
activities.prompt: Order what happens on a normal lookup.
items: PC checks its cache and hosts file
PC asks its configured DNS server
Resolver queries up the hierarchy if needed
Answer is cached for the TTL

rows.label: Command to clear the Windows DNS cache
Record type for the mail server
Cisco command that forwards DHCP broadcasts to a server on another subnet (two words)

hints: TTL controls how long an answer is cached.
labs.review: Match the symptom to the layer first: no address is DHCP, names failing while IPs work is DNS, and old answers are a cache or hosts-file problem.
